title: ReviewReport
description: Output schema for the multi-agent code review skill

scope.description: Description of what was reviewed (branch diff, staged files, directory)

verdict.description: Overall verdict, from the findings left open: ready = no critical or high open; needs-attention = a high open; needs-work = a critical open

id.description: Unique rule identifier with domain prefix

severity.description: critical: the app is broken or unsafe for every user, now. high: wrong runtime behaviour in a reachable case, or a resource leak. medium: correct today but will erode — duplication, a missing seam, an untested branch. low: readability, naming, documentation. A documentation or naming gap can NEVER be high: it cannot change what the program does.

file.description: Relative file path from project root

rule.description: Short rule name from reference guide

problem.description: What is wrong. State the defect, not the remedy.

suggestion.description: OPTIONAL. A remedy you have actually thought through. Omit it rather than guess: a wrong remedy is worse than none, because it gets applied. Two remedies were wrong on 2026-09-16 while both findings were right.

fix_prompt.description: Optional copy-pasteable instruction for the fixing agent

needs_verification.description: When true, the finding is ambiguous and must be confirmed via opensrc/ source or the web before fixing (e.g., deprecated three.js API, changed method signature)

verification_query.description: The query to run against opensrc/ or the web when needs_verification is true (e.g., 'three.js Raycaster intersectObject recursive default')

evidence.description: How you know. Quote the line, name the two places that disagree, or show the arithmetic. Any computed figure (a contrast ratio, a size, a count) MUST show its working so it can be re-derived.

confidence.description: confirmed: read it in the code and it cannot be otherwise. likely: strong inference, one assumption. speculative: worth a look, may be nothing. Say speculative rather than inflating.

what_breaks_if_fixed_naively.description: The trap in the obvious fix. Required whenever `suggestion` is present. Example from 2026-09-16: capping border segments to bound memory would have reintroduced the interrupted-border bug the code existed to abolish.

blast_radius.description: What else reads or writes the state this finding touches, and whether you checked it. The two worst bugs of 2026-09-16 were both outside the diff.

clean.description: A null result, stated so it can be trusted. A reviewer that never reports 'nothing' will eventually invent something.

checked.description: What was actually examined and found sound.

verdict.description: One line on the overall state of the dimension.
